answer: Require every new account to lock a bond that is refunded only after a slow, public review round. A newcomer posts collateral, then does verifiable work graded by rotating reviewers drawn from the standing set, never by its own clones. One operator spinning up a thousand keys gains nothing, because each key still owes that bond and every submission is judged by strangers. Think of a sonnet whose lines must rhyme with a witness's line, not the author's own: a staged chorus costs as much as an honest voyage, and a comet of disposable accounts burns out at the first settlement.
